pairs.source_text: C. Plinius Tacito suo s. Petis ut tibi avunculi mei exitum scribam, quo verius tradere posteris possis.
pairs.question: Quis a Plinio minore petivit ut avunculi sui exitum scriberet, quo verius posteris traderetur?
pairs.question_en: Who asked Pliny the Younger to write an account of his uncle's death, so that it could be handed down to posterity more truly?
pairs.derivation: Addressee fact: the letter is to Tacitus ('C. Plinius Tacito suo s.'), who had requested the account ('Petis ut ... scribam, quo verius tradere posteris possis'). Closed-book: it is famously to the historian Tacitus that Pliny described the elder Pliny's death and the Vesuvius eruption. Entity-anchored, single-name answer.

pairs.source_text: Petis ut tibi avunculi mei exitum scribam, quo verius tradere posteris possis.
pairs.question: Quo gradu necessitudinis vir ille, cuius mortem Plinius minor ad Tacitum perscripsit, scriptori coniunctus erat?
pairs.question_en: By what degree of kinship was the man whose death Pliny the Younger described to Tacitus related to the writer?
pairs.answer_en: He was his maternal uncle (his mother's brother).
pairs.derivation: Relationship fact: the dead man is 'avunculus meus' (Pliny the Younger's maternal uncle), i.e. Pliny the Elder; avunculus = mother's brother (Plinia was the Elder's sister). Closed-book, well-known; entity-anchored to both Plinys and the eruption.

pairs.source_text: Erat Miseni classemque imperio praesens regebat.
pairs.question: Cui rei Plinius maior, cum Vesuvius erumperet, Miseni praeerat?
pairs.question_en: What was Pliny the Elder in command of at Misenum when Vesuvius erupted?
pairs.answer_en: The fleet (he was prefect of the fleet).
pairs.derivation: Command fact: 'Erat Miseni classemque imperio praesens regebat' — he was at Misenum commanding the fleet (praefectus classis Misenensis). Entity-anchored to Pliny the Elder and Misenum; short answer; closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Nubes — incertum procul intuentibus ex quo monte; Vesuvium fuisse postea cognitum est — oriebatur, cuius similitudinem et formam non alia magis arbor quam pinus expresserit.
pairs.question: Ex quo monte nubem illam ortam esse postea cognitum esse Plinius tradit?
pairs.question_en: From which mountain does Pliny report it was afterwards recognized that the cloud had risen?
pairs.derivation: The eruption mountain: 'Vesuvium fuisse postea cognitum est.' Closed-book famous; entity-anchored, single place answer; the canonical fact of the letter.

pairs.source_text: Nonum Kal. Septembres hora fere septima mater mea indicat ei apparere nubem inusitata et magnitudine et specie.
pairs.question: Quo die mater Plinii minoris fratri suo nubem inusitatam apparere indicavit?
pairs.question_en: On what day did Pliny the Younger's mother point out to her brother the appearance of an extraordinary cloud?
pairs.answer_en: On the ninth day before the Kalends of September (24 August).
pairs.derivation: Date fact: 'Nonum Kal. Septembres' = a.d. IX Kal. Sept. = 24 August (AD 79), the traditional date of the eruption. The 'mater mea' (Pliny the Younger's mother) was sister of Pliny the Elder, hence 'fratri suo.' Entity-anchored, date answer; closed-book famous.

pairs.source_text: Nubes — incertum procul intuentibus ex quo monte; Vesuvium fuisse postea cognitum est — oriebatur, cuius similitudinem et formam non alia magis arbor quam pinus expresserit. Nam longissimo velut trunco elata in altum quibusdam ramis diffundebatur.
pairs.question: Cui arbori potissimum similem fuisse nubem e Vesuvio ortam Plinius scribit?
pairs.question_en: To what tree above all does Pliny say the cloud that rose from Vesuvius was most similar?
pairs.derivation: Famous simile: the eruption column shaped 'non alia magis arbor quam pinus' — a long trunk spreading into branches at the top (umbrella pine). Translatable (a tree, not wordplay), entity-anchored, short answer; one of the best-known images in Latin literature.

pairs.source_text: Egrediebatur domo; accipit codicillos Rectinae Tasci imminenti periculo exterritae — nam villa eius subiacebat, nec ulla nisi navibus fuga -: ut se tanto discrimini eriperet orabat.
pairs.question: Cuius mulieris codicillos accepit Plinius maior, quae perterrita ut se periculo eriperet orabat?
pairs.question_en: Whose written note did Pliny the Elder receive, a woman who in terror begged to be rescued from the danger?
pairs.derivation: Named appeal: 'accipit codicillos Rectinae Tasci ... ut se tanto discrimini eriperet orabat.' Rectina's message turned his scientific reconnaissance into a rescue mission. Entity-anchored named person, single answer.

pairs.source_text: Cunctatus paulum an retro flecteret, mox gubernatori ut ita faceret monenti 'Fortes' inquit 'fortuna iuvat: Pomponianum pete.'
pairs.question: Quem virum petere Plinius maior gubernatorem iussit, cum diceret 'fortes fortuna iuvat'?
pairs.question_en: Whom did Pliny the Elder order the helmsman to make for, saying 'fortune favors the brave'?
pairs.derivation: Named destination: 'Pomponianum pete' — he sailed on to join Pomponianus (at Stabiae). Entity-anchored named person; short answer; the maxim 'fortes fortuna iuvat' anchors the moment.

pairs.source_text: 'Fortes' inquit 'fortuna iuvat: Pomponianum pete.' Stabiis erat diremptus sinu medio — nam sensim circumactis curvatisque litoribus mare infunditur.
pairs.question: In quo oppido Pomponianus, ad quem Plinius maior navigavit ibique periit, morabatur?
pairs.question_en: In what town was Pomponianus staying, the man to whom Pliny the Elder sailed and where he died?
pairs.derivation: Place fact: 'Stabiis erat' (Pomponianus at Stabiae); the elder Pliny reached him there and the death narrative unfolds at Stabiae. Famous death place of Pliny the Elder; entity-anchored, single place answer.

pairs.source_text: Dubito, constantiam vocare an imprudentiam debeam — agebam enim duodevicensimum annum -: posco librum Titi Livi, et quasi per otium lego atque etiam ut coeperam excerpo.
pairs.question: Quotum aetatis annum agebat Plinius minor, cum Vesuvius erumperet?
pairs.question_en: Which year of his age was Pliny the Younger in when Vesuvius erupted?
pairs.derivation: Age fact: 'agebam enim duodevicensimum annum' — Pliny the Younger was in his eighteenth year at the eruption (AD 79). Entity-anchored, ordinal/number answer; closed-book.

pairs.source_text: posco librum Titi Livi, et quasi per otium lego atque etiam ut coeperam excerpo.
pairs.question: Cuius scriptoris librum Plinius minor, Vesuvio iam erumpente, poposcit et legebat?
pairs.question_en: Whose book did Pliny the Younger call for and read while Vesuvius was already erupting?
pairs.derivation: Famous detail: 'posco librum Titi Livi ... lego atque ... excerpo.' Entity-anchored to Pliny the Younger and Livy; single-name answer; closed-book.

pairs.source_text: Hic situs est Rufus, pulso qui Vindice quondam imperium asseruit non sibi sed patriae.
pairs.question: Quem Verginius Rufus, ut in epitaphio quod sibi composuit apud Plinium legitur, pepulisse se gloriatur?
pairs.question_en: Whom does Verginius Rufus boast, in the epitaph he composed for himself and recorded by Pliny, to have driven out?
pairs.derivation: Historical fact: in letter 6.10 about Verginius Rufus's tomb, his self-composed epitaph reads 'pulso ... Vindice' — having suppressed the revolt of Vindex (AD 68) he claimed empire 'not for himself but for the fatherland.' Entity-anchored, single-name answer; closed-book famous.

pairs.source_text: Accusavi Marium Priscum, qui lege repetundarum damnatus utebatur clementia legis, cuius severitatem immanitate criminum excesserat; relegatus est.
pairs.question: Quem virum Plinius lege repetundarum accusavit, qui damnatus relegatus est?
pairs.question_en: Whom did Pliny prosecute under the extortion law, a man who was condemned and relegated?
pairs.derivation: First-person fact: 'Accusavi Marium Priscum ... lege repetundarum damnatus ... relegatus est.' The celebrated extortion trial of Marius Priscus, proconsul of Africa. Entity-anchored to Pliny and Marius Priscus; single-name answer; closed-book.
